pattern: 〜ちゃいけない / 〜じゃいけない
meaning: Casual 'you mustn't': the spoken short form of 〜てはいけない. 〜ては becomes 〜ちゃ, and 〜では becomes 〜じゃ.

examples.ja: ここで{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}っ[[ちゃいけない]]よ。
examples.en: You can't take photos here.

examples.ja: {授業中|じゅぎょうちゅう}に{寝|ね}[[ちゃいけない]]よ。
examples.en: You mustn't sleep in class.

examples.ja: この{川|かわ}で{泳|およ}い[[じゃいけない]]よ。
examples.en: You can't swim in this river.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}はお{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}ん[[じゃいけない]]。
examples.en: Children mustn't drink alcohol.

questions.ja: テストの{時|とき}、ノートを[[{見|み}ちゃいけない]]よ。
questions.en: You mustn't look at your notes during the test.
questions.explain: 見る is an ichidan verb: 見て becomes 見ちゃ.

questions.ja: {道|みち}で[[{遊|あそ}んじゃいけない]]よ。
questions.en: You mustn't play in the street.
questions.explain: 遊ぶ becomes 遊んで, and a て-form ending in で turns into じゃ.

pattern: Noun / な-adj + だ / です
meaning: The copula 'is / am / are' after a noun or な-adjective. です is polite; だ is the plain form for friends and for writing.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{学生|がくせい}[[です]]。
examples.en: I'm a student.

examples.ja: あの{人|ひと}は{木村|きむら}さんのお{兄|にい}さん[[だ]]よ。
examples.en: That's Kimura's older brother.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}み[[です]]か。
examples.en: Is tomorrow a day off?

examples.ja: それは{私|わたし}の{傘|かさ}[[だ]]よ。
examples.en: That's my umbrella.

questions.ja: この{本|ほん}はとても{面白|おもしろ}い[[です]]。
questions.en: This book is very interesting.
questions.explain: い-adjectives take です to be polite, never だ; the past would be 面白かったです.

questions.ja: この{部屋|へや}はいつも{静|しず}か[[だ]]ね。
questions.en: This room is always quiet, isn't it?
questions.explain: In casual speech a な-adjective ends the sentence with だ; な only goes before a noun.

meaning: 'Only, just': limits things to what comes before it and nothing more.

examples.ja: {朝|あさ}はコーヒー[[だけ]]{飲|の}みます。
examples.en: In the morning I only drink coffee.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}は{少|すこ}し[[だけ]]{分|わ}かります。
examples.en: I understand just a little Japanese.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{日曜日|にちようび}[[だけ]]{休|やす}みです。
examples.en: This shop is closed only on Sundays.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}のパーティーには{一人|ひとり}[[だけ]]{来|き}ました。
examples.en: Only one person came to yesterday's party.

questions.ja: {財布|さいふ}に{千円|せんえん}[[だけ]]あります。
questions.en: I only have 1,000 yen in my wallet.
questions.explain: だけ goes with an affirmative verb; しか would need ありません.

questions.ja: すみません、{見|み}ている[[だけ]]です。
questions.en: Sorry, I'm just looking.
questions.explain: Verb + だけです means 'I'm only doing this'.

meaning: Plain form of でしょう: 'probably', or 'right?' when you expect the listener to agree. Used in casual speech and in writing.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}[[だろう]]。
examples.en: It'll probably rain tomorrow.

examples.ja: {木村|きむら}さんはもう{家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}った[[だろう]]。
examples.en: Kimura has probably gone home by now.

examples.ja: あの{店|みせ}は{高|たか}い[[だろう]]。
examples.en: That shop is probably expensive.

examples.ja: {一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}く[[だろう]]？
examples.en: You're coming with us, right?

questions.ja: {明日|あした}はたぶん{晴|は}れ[[だろう]]。
questions.en: It'll probably be sunny tomorrow.
questions.explain: だろう attaches straight to a noun, with no だ or な, and is never followed by です.

questions.ja: {木村|きむら}さんはもう{駅|えき}に{着|つ}い[[ただろう]]。
questions.en: Kimura has probably reached the station by now.
questions.explain: Put だろう after the plain past form: 着いた + だろう.

meaning: Marks where an action takes place, or the tool, language or transport used to do it.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}[[で]]{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みます。
examples.en: I read books at the library.

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}バス[[で]]{会社|かいしゃ}へ{行|い}きます。
examples.en: I go to work by bus every morning.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}[[で]]{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}きました。
examples.en: I wrote a letter in Japanese.

examples.ja: {箸|はし}[[で]]ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べます。
examples.en: I eat rice with chopsticks.

questions.ja: {食堂|しょくどう}[[で]]{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べました。
questions.en: I had lunch in the cafeteria.
questions.explain: The place where an action happens takes で.

questions.ja: {日本語|にほんご}[[で]]{話|はな}してください。
questions.en: Please speak in Japanese.
questions.explain: The language you speak in takes で.

meaning: 'But' or 'however' at the start of a sentence, setting it against the one before. Common in conversation.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}は{難|むずか}しいです。[[でも]]、{面白|おもしろ}いです。
examples.en: Japanese is hard. But it's interesting.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{雨|あめ}でした。[[でも]]、{公園|こうえん}へ{行|い}きました。
examples.en: It rained yesterday. But I went to the park anyway.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{安|やす}いです。[[でも]]、あまりおいしくないです。
examples.en: This place is cheap. But the food isn't very good.

examples.ja: {行|い}きたいです。[[でも]]、{時間|じかん}がありません。
examples.en: I want to go. But I don't have time.

questions.ja: この{靴|くつ}はとても{高|たか}いです。[[でも]]、{買|か}いました。
questions.en: These shoes are very expensive. But I bought them.
questions.explain: でも can open a sentence; から, ので and のに must attach to the end of a clause.

questions.ja: {兄|あに}は{背|せ}が{高|たか}いです。[[でも]]、{弟|おとうと}は{低|ひく}いです。
questions.en: My older brother is tall. But my younger brother is short.
questions.explain: Only でも can start a new sentence to show contrast.

meaning: 'Probably' when making a polite guess; with a rising tone, 'right?' to check that the listener agrees.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{晴|は}れる[[でしょう]]。
examples.en: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

examples.ja: {木村|きむら}さんは{来|こ}ない[[でしょう]]。
examples.en: Kimura probably won't come.

examples.ja: あのレストランは{高|たか}い[[でしょう]]ね。
examples.en: That restaurant must be expensive.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}、{面白|おもしろ}かった[[でしょう]]？
examples.en: This book was good, wasn't it?

questions.ja: {今晩|こんばん}は{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}る[[でしょう]]。
questions.en: It will probably snow tonight.
questions.explain: でしょう follows the plain form directly; ましょう means 'let's' and goes on a verb stem.

questions.ja: あの{人|ひと}はたぶん{学生|がくせい}[[でしょう]]。
questions.en: That person is probably a student.
questions.explain: でしょう attaches straight to a noun, with no だ or な.

meaning: 'What kind of…?': asks what something or someone is like. It always comes directly before a noun.

examples.ja: [[どんな]]{音楽|おんがく}が{好|す}きですか。
examples.en: What kind of music do you like?

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しいアパートは[[どんな]]{所|ところ}ですか。
examples.en: What's your new apartment like?

examples.ja: [[どんな]]スポーツをしますか。
examples.en: What sports do you play?

examples.ja: あなたの{町|まち}は[[どんな]]{町|まち}ですか。
examples.en: What's your town like?

questions.ja: [[どんな]]{食|た}べ{物|もの}が{好|す}きですか。
questions.en: What kind of food do you like?
questions.explain: どんな comes right before a noun to ask 'what kind of'.

questions.ja: {木村|きむら}さんのお{姉|ねえ}さんは[[どんな]]{人|ひと}ですか。
questions.en: What is Kimura's older sister like?
questions.explain: To ask what a person is like, use どんな + 人.

meaning: 'Why?': asks for a reason. The reply usually ends in 〜から or 〜からです.

examples.ja: [[どうして]]{昨日|きのう}{学校|がっこう}を{休|やす}んだんですか。
examples.en: Why were you off school yesterday?

examples.ja: [[どうして]]{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しているんですか。
examples.en: Why are you studying Japanese?

examples.ja: [[どうして]]{何|なに}も{食|た}べないんですか。
examples.en: Why aren't you eating anything?

examples.ja: 「[[どうして]]{傘|かさ}を{持|も}っているんですか。」「{午後|ごご}、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}るからです。」
examples.en: "Why have you got an umbrella?" "Because it's going to rain this afternoon."

questions.ja: 「[[どうして]]{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けたんですか。」「{暑|あつ}かったからです。」
questions.en: "Why did you open the window?" "Because it was hot."
questions.explain: The reply gives a reason (〜からです), so the question asks 'why'.

questions.ja: 「[[どうして]]{何|なに}も{言|い}わなかったんですか。」「よく{分|わ}からなかったからです。」
questions.en: "Why didn't you say anything?" "Because I didn't really understand."
questions.explain: The reply gives a reason, so the question needs どうして.

meaning: 'How?', 'by what means?': asks about the method or route for doing something.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}まで[[どうやって]]{行|い}きますか。
examples.en: How do I get to the station?

examples.ja: この{漢字|かんじ}は[[どうやって]]{読|よ}みますか。
examples.en: How do you read this kanji?

examples.ja: [[どうやって]]{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しましたか。
examples.en: How did you study Japanese?

examples.ja: このカメラは[[どうやって]]{使|つか}うんですか。
examples.en: How do you use this camera?

questions.ja: 「{会社|かいしゃ}まで[[どうやって]]{来|き}ますか。」「{自転車|じてんしゃ}で{来|き}ます。」
questions.en: "How do you get to work?" "I come by bike."
questions.explain: The reply gives a means (自転車で), so the question asks 'how'.

questions.ja: この{料理|りょうり}は[[どうやって]]{作|つく}りますか。
questions.en: How do you make this dish?
questions.explain: どうやって asks the method and goes before a verb; どんな needs a noun after it.

meaning: Marks the subject, especially new information or the answer to 'who?' or 'what?'. Also marks the object of words like 好き, 上手 and 分かる.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{猫|ねこ}[[が]]{好|す}きです。
examples.en: I like cats.

examples.ja: あ、{雨|あめ}[[が]]{降|ふ}っていますね。
examples.en: Oh, it's raining.

examples.ja: マリアさんは{英語|えいご}[[が]]{分|わ}かります。
examples.en: Maria understands English.

examples.ja: 「{誰|だれ}が{作|つく}りましたか。」「{母|はは}[[が]]{作|つく}りました。」
examples.en: "Who made it?" "My mother made it."

questions.ja: {誰|だれ}[[が]]この{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}きましたか。
questions.en: Who wrote this letter?
questions.explain: Question words like 誰 take が as the subject, never は.

questions.ja: {木村|きむら}さんはテニス[[が]]{上手|じょうず}です。
questions.en: Kimura is good at tennis.
questions.explain: 上手 marks the skill with が.

meaning: 'There is' or 'I have' for things and events. People and animals take います instead.

examples.ja: {机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}に{本|ほん}が[[あります]]。
examples.en: There's a book on the desk.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、テストが[[あります]]。
examples.en: I have a test tomorrow.

examples.ja: この{近|ちか}くに{銀行|ぎんこう}が[[あります]]か。
examples.en: Is there a bank near here?

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{時間|じかん}が[[ありません]]。
examples.en: I don't have time today.

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}にテレビが[[あります]]。
questions.en: There's a TV in the room.
questions.explain: A TV is a thing, so it takes あります.

questions.ja: {財布|さいふ}にお{金|かね}が[[ありません]]。
questions.en: There's no money in my wallet.
questions.explain: Money is a thing; the negative of あります is ありません.

meaning: 'I want (something)': for objects you'd like to have. ほしい conjugates like an い-adjective; for actions use 〜たい.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しいパソコンが[[ほしい]]です。
examples.en: I want a new computer.

examples.ja: {誕生日|たんじょうび}に{何|なに}が[[ほしい]]ですか。
examples.en: What do you want for your birthday?

examples.ja: {前|まえ}は{大|おお}きい{車|くるま}が[[ほしかった]]です。
examples.en: I used to want a big car.

examples.ja: {今|いま}は{何|なに}も[[ほしくない]]です。
examples.en: I don't want anything right now.

questions.ja: {子供|こども}の{時|とき}、{自転車|じてんしゃ}が[[ほしかったです]]。
questions.en: When I was a child, I wanted a bike.
questions.explain: ほしい is an い-adjective, so its past is ほしかったです.

questions.ja: もっと{広|ひろ}い{部屋|へや}が[[ほしいです]]。
questions.en: I want a bigger room.
questions.explain: For things you want, use ほしい; たい attaches to verbs.

meaning: 'There is' or 'I have' for people and animals. Things take あります.

examples.ja: {公園|こうえん}に{子供|こども}が[[います]]。
examples.en: There are children in the park.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{兄|あに}が{二人|ふたり}[[います]]。
examples.en: I have two older brothers.

examples.ja: {木|き}の{上|うえ}に{鳥|とり}が[[います]]。
examples.en: There's a bird up in the tree.

examples.ja: {教室|きょうしつ}に{先生|せんせい}が[[いません]]。
examples.en: The teacher isn't in the classroom.

questions.ja: {庭|にわ}に{猫|ねこ}が[[います]]。
questions.en: There's a cat in the garden.
questions.explain: A cat is alive, so it takes います.

questions.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}は{会社|かいしゃ}に{誰|だれ}も[[いません]]。
questions.en: There's nobody at the office on Sundays.
questions.explain: 誰も needs a negative, and people take いる: いません.

pattern: 〜たほうがいい / 〜ないほうがいい
meaning: 'You'd better' or 'it's best to': gives advice. Use the past form (〜た) to advise doing something and 〜ない to advise against it.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っていますから、タクシーで{行|い}った[[ほうがいい]]ですよ。
examples.en: It's raining, so you'd better take a taxi.

examples.ja: {夜|よる}はあまり{食|た}べない[[ほうがいい]]です。
examples.en: It's better not to eat much at night.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{寒|さむ}いですから、コートを{着|き}た[[ほうがいい]]ですよ。
examples.en: It's cold today, so you'd better wear a coat.

examples.ja: {疲|つか}れている{時|とき}は、{早|はや}く{寝|ね}た[[ほうがいい]]です。
examples.en: When you're tired, it's best to go to bed early.

questions.ja: {風邪|かぜ}ですか。{薬|くすり}を[[{飲|の}んだ]]ほうがいいですよ。
questions.en: Have you got a cold? You'd better take some medicine.
questions.explain: To advise doing something, use the past た-form + ほうがいい.

questions.ja: {危|あぶ}ないですから、この{川|かわ}で[[{泳|およ}がない]]ほうがいいです。
questions.en: It's dangerous, so you'd better not swim in this river.
questions.explain: To advise against something, use the ない-form: 泳ぐ becomes 泳がない.

pattern: 〜い / 〜くない / 〜かった / 〜くなかった
meaning: Adjectives ending in い change that ending for negative and past: 高い, 高くない, 高かった, 高くなかった. いい works from よい: よくない, よかった.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}はとても[[{暑|あつ}い]]です。
examples.en: It's very hot today.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}はあまり[[{広|ひろ}くない]]です。
examples.en: This room isn't very big.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}のテストは[[{難|むずか}しかった]]です。
examples.en: Yesterday's test was difficult.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}はとても[[よかった]]です。
examples.en: The trip was really good.

questions.ja: {昨日|きのう}はとても[[{寒|さむ}かったです]]。
questions.en: It was very cold yesterday.
questions.explain: The past of 寒い is 寒かった; い-adjectives never take でした.

questions.ja: この{映画|えいが}はあまり[[よくなかったです]]。
questions.en: This film wasn't very good.
wrong: いいじゃなかったです
questions.explain: いい conjugates from よい: よくない, よかった, よくなかった.

meaning: 'Most', 'number one': marks the top of a group, often with 〜の中で or 〜で.

examples.ja: {家族|かぞく}の{中|なか}で{父|ちち}が[[{一番|いちばん}]]{背|せ}が{高|たか}いです。
examples.en: My father is the tallest in my family.

examples.ja: スポーツの{中|なか}でサッカーが[[{一番|いちばん}]]{好|す}きです。
examples.en: Of all sports, I like football the most.

examples.ja: {一年|いちねん}で{八月|はちがつ}が[[{一番|いちばん}]]{暑|あつ}いです。
examples.en: August is the hottest month of the year.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}で[[{一番|いちばん}]]{安|やす}いのはどれですか。
examples.en: Which is the cheapest one in this shop?

questions.ja: クラスで{木村|きむら}さんが[[{一番|いちばん}]]{若|わか}いです。
questions.en: Kimura is the youngest in the class.
questions.explain: Within a group, the top one is marked with 一番.

questions.ja: {日本|にほん}の{料理|りょうり}で{何|なに}が[[{一番|いちばん}]]{好|す}きですか。
questions.en: What's your favourite Japanese dish?
questions.explain: 一番 + 好き asks which one you like the most.

pattern: Person + と + 一緒に + Verb
meaning: 'Together (with)': doing something along with someone, who is marked with と.

examples.ja: {友達|ともだち}と[[{一緒|いっしょ}に]]{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
examples.en: I watched a film with a friend.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、[[{一緒|いっしょ}に]]{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べませんか。
examples.en: Shall we have lunch together tomorrow?

examples.ja: {毎晩|まいばん}、{家族|かぞく}と[[{一緒|いっしょ}に]]テレビを{見|み}ます。
examples.en: Every evening I watch TV with my family.

examples.ja: {犬|いぬ}と[[{一緒|いっしょ}に]]{公園|こうえん}を{歩|ある}きます。
examples.en: I walk in the park with my dog.

questions.ja: {母|はは}[[と]]{一緒|いっしょ}に{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}きました。
questions.en: I went shopping with my mother.
questions.explain: The person you do something with is marked with と.

questions.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}、{友達|ともだち}と[[{一緒|いっしょ}に]]テニスをしました。
questions.en: On Sunday I played tennis with a friend.
questions.explain: 一緒 needs に to work with a verb: 一緒に.

meaning: 'Always' or 'usually': something that happens every time or as a regular habit.

examples.ja: {朝|あさ}は[[いつも]]パンを{食|た}べます。
examples.en: I always have bread in the morning.

examples.ja: {木村|きむら}さんは[[いつも]]{元気|げんき}ですね。
examples.en: Kimura is always so cheerful.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は[[いつも]]11{時|じ}に{寝|ね}ます。
examples.en: I always go to bed at eleven.

examples.ja: [[いつも]]{駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}いて{行|い}きます。
examples.en: I always walk to the station.

questions.ja: {父|ちち}は[[いつも]]{朝|あさ}6{時|じ}に{起|お}きます。
questions.en: My father always gets up at six in the morning.
questions.explain: あまり and ぜんぜん need a negative; いつも fits a regular habit.

questions.ja: [[いつも]]{何時|なんじ}に{寝|ね}ますか。
questions.en: What time do you usually go to bed?
questions.explain: いつも in a question asks about your usual habit.

pattern: Noun / な-adj + じゃない / ではない
meaning: 'Is not': the negative of だ / です after a noun or な-adjective. じゃない is spoken and ではない more formal; the polite forms end in ありません.

examples.ja: これは{私|わたし}のかばん[[じゃない]]よ。
examples.en: This isn't my bag.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{医者|いしゃ}[[ではありません]]。
examples.en: My father isn't a doctor.

examples.ja: この{辺|へん}はあまり{静|しず}か[[じゃない]]です。
examples.en: This area isn't very quiet.

examples.ja: それは{本当|ほんとう}[[ではない]]。
examples.en: That is not true.

questions.ja: {木村|きむら}さんは{日本人|にほんじん}[[じゃありません]]。
questions.en: Kimura isn't Japanese.
questions.explain: Nouns are negated with じゃありません, never with く.

questions.ja: この{町|まち}は{有名|ゆうめい}[[じゃない]]です。
questions.en: This town isn't famous.
questions.explain: な-adjectives take じゃない; くない is only for い-adjectives.

meaning: At the end of a sentence it makes a question. Between two nouns it means 'or', and after a question word it means 'some-' (誰か, 何か).

examples.ja: これは{何|なん}です[[か]]。
examples.en: What is this?

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、{学校|がっこう}に{来|き}ます[[か]]。
examples.en: Are you coming to school tomorrow?

examples.ja: コーヒー[[か]]{紅茶|こうちゃ}をください。
examples.en: Coffee or tea, please.

examples.ja: {誰|だれ}[[か]]{来|き}ましたよ。
examples.en: Someone's here.

questions.ja: あの{人|ひと}は{誰|だれ}です[[か]]。
questions.en: Who is that person?
questions.explain: か at the end turns the sentence into a question.

questions.ja: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}に{何|なに}[[か]]ありますか。
questions.en: Is there anything in the fridge?
questions.explain: 何か means 'something'; 何も would need a negative.

meaning: 'A or B': lists choices for the listener to pick from. With a verb and its negative it means 'whether or not'.

examples.ja: {肉|にく}か{魚|さかな}[[か]]、どちらがいいですか。
examples.en: Meat or fish, which would you like?

examples.ja: {行|い}く[[か]]{行|い}かないか、まだ{分|わ}かりません。
examples.en: I don't know yet whether I'll go or not.

examples.ja: {土曜日|どようび}[[か]]{日曜日|にちようび}か、どちらが{暇|ひま}ですか。
examples.en: Which day are you free, Saturday or Sunday?

questions.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}[[か]]バスか、どちらで{行|い}きますか。
questions.en: Train or bus, which will you take?
questions.explain: AかBか lists the choices; the first か follows A.

questions.ja: {明日|あした}{来|く}る[[か]]{来|こ}ないか、{電話|でんわ}で{教|おし}えてください。
questions.en: Please call and tell me whether you're coming tomorrow or not.
questions.explain: Verb + か + its negative + か means 'whether or not'.

meaning: After a reason: 'because, so'. After a noun, place or time: 'from', the starting point.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っています[[から]]、{傘|かさ}を{持|も}って{行|い}きます。
examples.en: It's raining, so I'll take an umbrella.

examples.ja: {暑|あつ}い[[から]]、{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けましょう。
examples.en: It's hot, so let's open the window.

examples.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みは{来週|らいしゅう}[[から]]です。
examples.en: The summer holidays start next week.

examples.ja: {家|いえ}[[から]]{駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}いて10{分|ぷん}です。
examples.en: It's a ten-minute walk from my house to the station.

questions.ja: {仕事|しごと}は{朝|あさ}9{時|じ}[[から]]{夕方|ゆうがた}5{時|じ}までです。
questions.en: Work is from 9 in the morning until 5 in the evening.
questions.explain: から marks the starting time; まで marks the end.

questions.ja: {疲|つか}れた[[から]]、{少|すこ}し{休|やす}みましょう。
questions.en: I'm tired, so let's take a short break.
questions.explain: から after a clause gives the reason.

meaning: Verb stem + 方 means 'how to do' or 'the way of doing' it: 読み方, 使い方.

examples.ja: この{漢字|かんじ}の{読|よ}み[[{方|かた}]]を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.en: Please tell me how to read this kanji.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}への{行|い}き[[{方|かた}]]が{分|わ}かりません。
examples.en: I don't know how to get to the station.

examples.ja: {母|はは}にカレーの{作|つく}り[[{方|かた}]]を{習|なら}いました。
examples.en: My mother taught me how to make curry.

examples.ja: このカメラの{使|つか}い[[{方|かた}]]は{難|むずか}しいです。
examples.en: This camera is hard to use.

questions.ja: {日本|にほん}の{手紙|てがみ}の[[{書|か}き{方|かた}]]を{習|なら}いたいです。
questions.en: I want to learn how to write a Japanese letter.
questions.explain: 方 attaches to the ます-stem: 書きます becomes 書き方.

questions.ja: この{果物|くだもの}の[[{食|た}べ{方|かた}]]を{知|し}っていますか。
questions.en: Do you know how to eat this fruit?
questions.explain: For ichidan verbs, drop る and add 方: 食べ方.

meaning: 'But', 'though': joins two contrasting clauses. Casual and very common; it also softens a request or introduces a topic.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{高|たか}い[[けど]]、おいしいです。
examples.en: This place is expensive, but the food is good.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しています[[けど]]、まだ{下手|へた}です。
examples.en: I'm studying Japanese, but I'm still not good at it.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}{映画|えいが}に{行|い}きます[[けど]]、{一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}きませんか。
examples.en: I'm going to a film tomorrow. Would you like to come?

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{寒|さむ}かった[[けど]]、{今日|きょう}は{暖|あたた}かいね。
examples.en: It was cold yesterday, but today's warm, isn't it?

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}は{狭|せま}い[[けど]]、{駅|えき}から{近|ちか}いです。
questions.en: The room is small, but it's close to the station.
questions.explain: けど attaches straight to the plain form; い-adjectives never take だ.

questions.ja: {今日|きょう}は{日曜日|にちようび}だ[[けど]]、{仕事|しごと}に{行|い}きます。
questions.en: It's Sunday today, but I'm going to work.
questions.explain: After a noun, けど follows だ: 日曜日だけど.

meaning: 'But', 'although': the fuller, more polite form of けど, used in careful speech and writing. けれど sits in between.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}の{夏|なつ}は{暑|あつ}いです[[けれども]]、{好|す}きです。
examples.en: Japanese summers are hot, but I like them.

examples.ja: {何回|なんかい}も{読|よ}みました[[けれども]]、よく{分|わ}かりませんでした。
examples.en: I read it many times, but I didn't really understand it.

examples.ja: すみません[[けれども]]、{少|すこ}し{待|ま}ってください。
examples.en: I'm sorry, but please wait a moment.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}です[[けれど]]、{私|わたし}は{下手|へた}です。
examples.en: My brother is good at cooking, but I'm bad at it.

questions.ja: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}みました[[けれども]]、まだ{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}いです。
questions.en: I took some medicine, but I still have a headache.
questions.explain: けれども follows the ます-form directly to show contrast.

questions.ja: {木村|きむら}さんは{学生|がくせい}です[[けれども]]、{毎日|まいにち}{仕事|しごと}をしています。
questions.en: Kimura is a student, but he works every day.
questions.explain: けれども can follow です to join two contrasting clauses.

meaning: With an affirmative verb, 'still'; with a negative, or as まだです, 'not yet'.

examples.ja: {外|そと}は[[まだ]]{明|あか}るいです。
examples.en: It's still light outside.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}たちは[[まだ]]{寝|ね}ています。
examples.en: The children are still asleep.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は[[まだ]]{学生|がくせい}です。
examples.en: My older brother is still a student.

examples.ja: コーヒーが[[まだ]]{少|すこ}しあります。
examples.en: There's still a little coffee left.

questions.ja: {雨|あめ}が[[まだ]]{降|ふ}っています。
questions.en: It's still raining.
questions.explain: With an affirmative verb, まだ means 'still'.

questions.ja: 「{宿題|しゅくだい}はもう{終|お}わりましたか。」「いいえ、[[まだ]]です。」
questions.en: "Have you finished your homework?" "No, not yet."
questions.explain: いいえ、まだです is the short answer for 'not yet'.

pattern: まだ + Verb-て + いません
meaning: 'Haven't done it yet': for something that hasn't happened so far but still might. The usual answer to もう〜ましたか.

examples.ja: {宿題|しゅくだい}はまだし[[ていません]]。
examples.en: I haven't done my homework yet.

examples.ja: {木村|きむら}さんはまだ{来|き}[[ていません]]。
examples.en: Kimura hasn't arrived yet.

examples.ja: その{映画|えいが}はまだ{見|み}[[ていません]]。
examples.en: I haven't seen that film yet.

examples.ja: {手紙|てがみ}はまだ{書|か}い[[ていません]]。
examples.en: I haven't written the letter yet.

questions.ja: 「もう{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べましたか。」「いいえ、まだ{食|た}べ[[ていません]]。」
questions.en: "Have you had lunch yet?" "No, not yet."
questions.explain: 'Not yet' uses まだ + 〜ていません, not the past negative.

questions.ja: {新|あたら}しい{漢字|かんじ}はまだ{覚|おぼ}え[[ていません]]。
questions.en: I haven't learned the new kanji yet.
questions.explain: まだ + 〜ていません: 覚える becomes 覚えていません.

meaning: Until, as far as: marks where a time, a distance or a range ends. Often paired with から (from).

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}9{時|じ}から5{時|じ}[[まで]]{働|はたら}きます。
examples.en: I work from nine to five every day.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}[[まで]]{歩|ある}いて10{分|ぷん}です。
examples.en: It's a ten-minute walk to the station.

examples.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みは{来週|らいしゅう}の{金曜日|きんようび}[[まで]]です。
examples.en: The summer holidays last until next Friday.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{夜遅|よるおそ}く[[まで]]{勉強|べんきょう}しました。
examples.en: Yesterday I studied until late at night.

questions.ja: {朝|あさ}から{晩|ばん}[[まで]]{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っていました。
questions.en: It rained from morning till night.
questions.explain: から〜まで marks a span: from one point until another.

questions.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}が{来|く}る[[まで]]、ここで{待|ま}ちましょう。
questions.en: Let's wait here until the train comes.
questions.explain: まで goes with an action that lasts up to a point, like waiting; までに means 'by' a deadline.

pattern: Verb (dictionary form) + 前に / Noun + の前に
meaning: Before: the first action happens before the second. The verb before 前に stays in dictionary form even in a past sentence; nouns take の前に.

examples.ja: {寝|ね}る[[{前|まえ}に]]{歯|は}を{磨|みが}きます。
examples.en: I brush my teeth before I go to bed.

examples.ja: {食|た}べる[[{前|まえ}に]]{手|て}を{洗|あら}いましょう。
examples.en: Let's wash our hands before we eat.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}へ{来|く}る[[{前|まえ}に]]、{少|すこ}し{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しました。
examples.en: I studied a little Japanese before I came to Japan.

examples.ja: {授業|じゅぎょう}の[[{前|まえ}に]]{宿題|しゅくだい}を{出|だ}してください。
examples.en: Please hand in your homework before class.

questions.ja: {昨日|きのう}は[[{寝|ね}る]]{前|まえ}に{少|すこ}し{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みました。
questions.en: Last night I read a little before going to sleep.
questions.explain: 前に always follows the dictionary form, even when the sentence is in the past.

questions.ja: {家|いえ}を{出|で}る[[{前|まえ}に]]、{電気|でんき}を{消|け}します。
questions.en: I turn off the lights before I leave the house.
questions.explain: Dictionary form + 前に means 'before doing'; 前で is a place, 'in front of'.

meaning: Won't you…? / Would you like to…?: a polite, soft invitation that makes it easy for the other person to say no.

examples.ja: {一緒|いっしょ}に{映画|えいが}を{見|み}[[ませんか]]。
examples.en: Would you like to see a film together?

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}、{公園|こうえん}を{散歩|さんぽ}し[[ませんか]]。
examples.en: How about a walk in the park on Sunday?

examples.ja: ちょっと{休|やす}み[[ませんか]]。
examples.en: Why don't we take a short break?

examples.ja: {今晩|こんばん}、うちでご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べ[[ませんか]]。
examples.en: Would you like to have dinner at my place tonight?

questions.ja: {明日|あした}、{一緒|いっしょ}に{図書館|としょかん}へ[[{行|い}きませんか]]。
questions.en: Would you like to go to the library with me tomorrow?
questions.explain: ませんか attaches to the ます-stem (行き), and an invitation about tomorrow can't be past.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}の{家|いえ}に{遊|あそ}びに{来|き}[[ませんか]]。
questions.en: Would you like to come over to my place?
questions.explain: Only the listener can come to the speaker's home, so it has to be an invitation: ませんか.

meaning: Let's…: a polite way to suggest doing something together, or to agree to a plan someone has offered.

examples.ja: もう{遅|おそ}いですから、{帰|かえ}り[[ましょう]]。
examples.en: It's late, so let's go home.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}の{前|まえ}で{会|あ}い[[ましょう]]。
examples.en: Let's meet in front of the station.

examples.ja: {一緒|いっしょ}に{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}を{作|つく}り[[ましょう]]。
examples.en: Let's make dinner together.

examples.ja: {次|つぎ}の{問題|もんだい}をやり[[ましょう]]。
examples.en: Let's do the next question.

questions.ja: 「{一緒|いっしょ}に{帰|かえ}りませんか。」「ええ、{帰|かえ}り[[ましょう]]。」
questions.en: "Shall we go home together?" "Yes, let's."
questions.explain: To say yes to an invitation, answer with ましょう: 'yes, let's'.

questions.ja: では、10ページを[[{読|よ}みましょう]]。
questions.en: Right, let's read page 10.
questions.explain: ましょう attaches to the ます-stem: 読む becomes 読み.

meaning: Shall I…? / Shall we…?: offers to do something for someone, or asks what to do together.

examples.ja: その{荷物|にもつ}、{持|も}ち[[ましょうか]]。
examples.en: Shall I carry that bag for you?

examples.ja: {暑|あつ}いですね。{窓|まど}を{開|あ}け[[ましょうか]]。
examples.en: It's hot, isn't it? Shall I open the window?

examples.ja: どこで{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べ[[ましょうか]]。
examples.en: Where shall we have lunch?

examples.ja: {写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}り[[ましょうか]]。
examples.en: Shall I take a photo of you?

questions.ja: {私|わたし}が{窓|まど}を{閉|し}め[[ましょうか]]。
questions.en: Shall I close the window?
questions.explain: With 私が the speaker is offering to do it, so ましょうか fits.

questions.ja: {何時|なんじ}に{駅|えき}で{会|あ}い[[ましょうか]]。
questions.en: What time shall we meet at the station?
questions.explain: A question word plus ましょうか asks the other person to help decide a plan.

meaning: Too, also; with a negative, (not) either. It takes the place of は, が or を. A question word + も + negative means nobody or nothing.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}[[も]]コーヒーが{好|す}きです。
examples.en: I like coffee too.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{肉|にく}も{魚|さかな}[[も]]{食|た}べません。
examples.en: My older brother eats neither meat nor fish.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{何|なに}[[も]]{食|た}べませんでした。
examples.en: I didn't eat anything yesterday.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}で1{時間|じかん}[[も]]{待|ま}ちました。
examples.en: I waited at the station for a whole hour.

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}には{誰|だれ}[[も]]いませんでした。
questions.en: There was nobody in the room.
questions.explain: Question word + も + a negative verb means 'nobody' or 'nothing'.

questions.ja: {父|ちち}も{母|はは}[[も]]{元気|げんき}です。
questions.en: Both my father and my mother are well.
questions.explain: AもBも means 'both A and B'; the second noun takes も as well.

meaning: Already, with a finished action; not … any more, with a negative. Before an amount it means 'more': もう一つ, もう少し.

examples.ja: {宿題|しゅくだい}は[[もう]]{終|お}わりました。
examples.en: I've already finished my homework.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}は[[もう]]{出|で}ましたか。
examples.en: Has the train already left?

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は[[もう]]たばこを{吸|す}いません。
examples.en: My father doesn't smoke any more.

examples.ja: [[もう]]{一|ひと}つください。
examples.en: One more, please.

questions.ja: {昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}は[[もう]]{食|た}べましたか。
questions.en: Have you had lunch yet?
questions.explain: もう with a past verb asks whether something has already happened; まだ, あまり and ぜんぜん don't fit a finished action.

questions.ja: すみません、[[もう]]{少|すこ}しゆっくり{話|はな}してください。
questions.en: Excuse me, could you speak a little more slowly?
questions.explain: もう少し is the set way to say 'a little more'.

pattern: な-adjective + な + Noun / な-adjective + です
meaning: Adjectives like 静か, 有名 and 便利. They take な before a noun and work like nouns at the end of a sentence: 静かです, 静かじゃない, 静かでした.

examples.ja: {静|しず}か[[な]]{町|まち}に{住|す}みたいです。
examples.en: I want to live in a quiet town.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}はあまりきれい[[じゃない]]です。
examples.en: This room isn't very clean.

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}の{公園|こうえん}はとてもにぎやか[[でした]]。
examples.en: The park was really lively on Sunday.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{魚|さかな}が{嫌|きら}い[[じゃありません]]。
examples.en: I don't dislike fish.

questions.ja: ここは{有名|ゆうめい}[[な]]レストランです。
questions.en: This is a famous restaurant.
questions.explain: A な-adjective takes な before a noun.

questions.ja: {先週|せんしゅう}は{仕事|しごと}が{大変|たいへん}[[でした]]。
questions.en: Work was tough last week.
questions.explain: In the past, a な-adjective takes でした, like a noun; かった is for い-adjectives.

meaning: A casual exclamation or sigh, often said to yourself: 'Wow…', 'Man…'. After たい it sounds wistful: 'I'd love to…'.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}のケーキ、おいしい[[なあ]]。
examples.en: The cake at this place is so good.

examples.ja: {仕事|しごと}が{忙|いそが}しい[[なあ]]。
examples.en: Man, work is busy.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}に{行|い}きたい[[なあ]]。
examples.en: I'd really love to go to Japan.

examples.ja: {大|おお}きい{家|いえ}だ[[なあ]]。
examples.en: What a big house!

questions.ja: いい{天気|てんき}[[だなあ]]。
questions.en: What lovely weather.
questions.explain: After a noun, なあ needs だ in front of it: 天気だなあ.

questions.ja: この{部屋|へや}、[[{寒|さむ}いなあ]]。
questions.en: This room is freezing.
questions.explain: An い-adjective takes なあ straight after い, with no だ.

meaning: Without doing: you do the main action and skip the first one, like going out without an umbrella.

examples.ja: {朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べ[[ないで]]{学校|がっこう}へ{行|い}きました。
examples.en: I went to school without eating breakfast.

examples.ja: {傘|かさ}を{持|も}た[[ないで]]{出|で}かけました。
examples.en: I went out without an umbrella.

examples.ja: {辞書|じしょ}を{使|つか}わ[[ないで]]この{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みました。
examples.en: I read this book without using a dictionary.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{寝|ね}[[ないで]]{勉強|べんきょう}しました。
examples.en: Yesterday I studied without sleeping.

questions.ja: {歯|は}を{磨|みが}か[[ないで]]{寝|ね}ました。
questions.en: I went to bed without brushing my teeth.
questions.explain: ないで joins a skipped action to the main verb: 'without doing'.

questions.ja: {何|なに}も[[{言|い}わないで]]{帰|かえ}りました。
questions.en: He went home without saying anything.
questions.explain: 言う is a godan verb, so its ない-form is 言わない; なくて can't mean 'without'.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + ないでください
meaning: Please don't…: a polite request asking someone not to do something.

examples.ja: ここで{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}ら[[ないでください]]。
examples.en: Please don't take photos here.

examples.ja: {教室|きょうしつ}で{食|た}べ[[ないでください]]。
examples.en: Please don't eat in the classroom.

examples.ja: この{話|はなし}は{誰|だれ}にも{言|い}わ[[ないでください]]。
examples.en: Please don't tell anyone about this.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{授業|じゅぎょう}を{忘|わす}れ[[ないでください]]。
examples.en: Please don't forget tomorrow's class.

questions.ja: {危|あぶ}ないですから、この{川|かわ}で{泳|およ}が[[ないでください]]。
questions.en: It's dangerous, so please don't swim in this river.
questions.explain: The polite 'please don't' is the ない-form + でください.

questions.ja: ここは{図書館|としょかん}ですから、{大|おお}きい{声|こえ}で[[{話|はな}さないでください]]。
questions.en: This is a library, so please don't talk loudly.
questions.explain: 話す is a godan verb: its ない-form is 話さない.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + ないといけない
meaning: Have to, must: literally 'if I don't, it won't do'. Very common in everyday speech.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は6{時|じ}に{起|お}き[[ないといけません]]。
examples.en: I have to get up at six tomorrow.

examples.ja: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}ま[[ないといけません]]。
examples.en: I have to take my medicine.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{部屋|へや}を{掃除|そうじ}し[[ないといけません]]。
examples.en: I need to clean my room today.

examples.ja: もう{帰|かえ}ら[[ないといけません]]。
examples.en: I have to go home now.

questions.ja: {明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}は{早|はや}いですから、{今日|きょう}は{早|はや}く{寝|ね}[[ないといけません]]。
questions.en: I have an early start tomorrow, so I have to go to bed early tonight.
questions.explain: The pattern is the ない-form + と + いけません.

questions.ja: {財布|さいふ}を{忘|わす}れました。{家|いえ}に[[{帰|かえ}らないといけません]]。
questions.en: I've left my wallet behind. I have to go back home.
wrong: {帰|かえ}りないといけません
{帰|かえ}るないといけません
questions.explain: 帰る looks like an ichidan verb but is godan, so its ない-form is 帰らない.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + なくてもいい(です)
meaning: Don't have to, needn't: says that something isn't necessary.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{学校|がっこう}へ{来|こ}[[なくてもいいです]]。
examples.en: You don't have to come to school tomorrow.

examples.ja: {靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}が[[なくてもいいです]]よ。
examples.en: You don't need to take your shoes off.

examples.ja: {全部|ぜんぶ}は{食|た}べ[[なくてもいいです]]。
examples.en: You don't have to eat all of it.

examples.ja: {名前|なまえ}は{書|か}か[[なくてもいい]]ですか。
examples.en: Is it all right if I don't write my name?

questions.ja: {今日|きょう}は{日曜日|にちようび}ですから、{早|はや}く{起|お}き[[なくてもいいです]]。
questions.en: It's Sunday today, so I don't have to get up early.
questions.explain: 'Don't have to' is the ない-form with い dropped + くてもいい.

questions.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っていませんから、{傘|かさ}は[[{持|も}たなくてもいいです]]よ。
questions.en: It isn't raining, so you don't need to take an umbrella.
questions.explain: 持つ is godan: 持たない becomes 持たなくてもいい.

meaning: Gotta, have to: a casual spoken shortening of なくては(いけない). The いけない part is usually left off.

examples.ja: あ、もう8{時|じ}だ。{行|い}か[[なくちゃ]]。
examples.en: Oh, it's already eight. I've got to go.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}テストだから、{勉強|べんきょう}し[[なくちゃ]]。
examples.en: I've got a test tomorrow, so I need to study.

examples.ja: {牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}がない。{買|か}わ[[なくちゃ]]。
examples.en: We're out of milk. I need to buy some.

examples.ja: {母|はは}に{電話|でんわ}し[[なくちゃ]]いけない。
examples.en: I have to call my mum.

questions.ja: もう{遅|おそ}いから、{帰|かえ}ら[[なくちゃ]]。
questions.en: It's late, so I've got to head home.
questions.explain: なくちゃ is a squeezed なくては: the ない-form with い dropped + くちゃ.

questions.ja: {明日|あした}は{早|はや}く[[{起|お}きなくちゃ]]。
questions.en: I've got to get up early tomorrow.
questions.explain: 起きる is ichidan: drop る to get 起きない, then 起きなくちゃ.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + なくてはいけない
meaning: Must, have to: something is required, by a rule or by the situation.

examples.ja: {学生|がくせい}は{宿題|しゅくだい}をし[[なくてはいけません]]。
examples.en: Students have to do their homework.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}の{本|ほん}を{返|かえ}さ[[なくてはいけません]]。
examples.en: I have to return the library books.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}では{家|いえ}に{入|はい}る{時|とき}、{靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}が[[なくてはいけません]]。
examples.en: In Japan you have to take your shoes off when you go into a house.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}はこの{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}か[[なくてはいけません]]。
examples.en: I have to write this letter today.

questions.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}る{時|とき}は、{切符|きっぷ}を{買|か}わ[[なくてはいけません]]。
questions.en: You have to buy a ticket when you take the train.
questions.explain: 'Must' is the ない-form with い dropped + くてはいけません.

questions.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}も{仕事|しごと}を[[しなくてはいけません]]。
questions.en: I have to work on Sundays too.
wrong: さなくてはいけません
すなくてはいけません
しなくてもいけません
questions.explain: The ない-form of する is しない, so it becomes しなくてはいけません.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + なくてはならない
meaning: Must, have to: means the same as なくてはいけない but sounds stiffer. Used for duties and rules, and in writing.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}は{学校|がっこう}へ{行|い}か[[なくてはなりません]]。
examples.en: Children must go to school.

examples.ja: {外国|がいこく}へ{行|い}く{時|とき}は、パスポートを{持|も}って{行|い}か[[なくてはなりません]]。
examples.en: When you travel abroad, you must take your passport.

examples.ja: {会社|かいしゃ}には9{時|じ}に{着|つ}か[[なくてはなりません]]。
examples.en: I have to be at the office at nine.

examples.ja: {借|か}りたお{金|かね}は{返|かえ}さ[[なくてはなりません]]。
examples.en: Money you borrow must be paid back.

questions.ja: {病院|びょういん}の{中|なか}では{静|しず}かにし[[なくてはなりません]]。
questions.en: You must keep quiet inside the hospital.
questions.explain: The pattern ends in なりません, the polite negative of なる.

questions.ja: {次|つぎ}のバスまで、ここで[[{待|ま}たなくてはなりません]]。
questions.en: I have to wait here until the next bus.
wrong: {待|ま}ちなくてはなりません
{待|ま}つなくてはなりません
{待|ま}たないてはなりません
questions.explain: 待つ is godan: 待たない becomes 待たなくてはなりません.

pattern: Noun / な-adjective + になる, い-adjective (〜く) + なる
meaning: To become: shows a change. Nouns and な-adjectives take に (医者になる, 静かになる); い-adjectives change い to く (暗くなる).

examples.ja: {春|はる}になって、{暖|あたた}か[[くなりました]]。
examples.en: Spring has come and it's got warmer.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{医者|いしゃ}[[になりました]]。
examples.en: My older brother became a doctor.

examples.ja: {部屋|へや}を{掃除|そうじ}して、きれい[[になりました]]。
examples.en: I cleaned the room and now it's tidy.

examples.ja: {来月|らいげつ}、20{歳|さい}[[になります]]。
examples.en: I'll turn twenty next month.

questions.ja: {夕方|ゆうがた}、{空|そら}が{暗|くら}[[くなりました]]。
questions.en: In the evening the sky got dark.
questions.explain: An い-adjective changes い to く before なる: 暗い becomes 暗くなる.

questions.ja: {子供|こども}たちが{寝|ね}て、{家|いえ}が{静|しず}か[[になりました]]。
questions.en: The children went to sleep and the house went quiet.
questions.explain: A な-adjective takes に before なる: 静かになる.

pattern: Plain form + んです (Noun / な-adjective + なんです)
meaning: Explains, or asks about, the reason or background: 'the thing is…', 'is it that…?'. Conversational; nouns and な-adjectives take なんです.

examples.ja: {頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}い[[んです]]。
examples.en: I've got a headache, you see.

examples.ja: どうして{食|た}べない[[んですか]]。
examples.en: Why aren't you eating?

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{誕生日|たんじょうび}な[[んです]]。
examples.en: It's my birthday today, actually.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}はパーティーに{行|い}きませんでした。{仕事|しごと}が{忙|いそが}しかった[[んです]]。
examples.en: I didn't go to the party yesterday. Work was busy.

questions.ja: {遅|おそ}くなってすみません。{電車|でんしゃ}が{来|こ}なかった[[んです]]。
questions.en: Sorry I'm late. The train didn't come.
questions.explain: After a verb, んです attaches directly; な is only for nouns and な-adjectives.

questions.ja: {今日|きょう}は{遊|あそ}びません。{明日|あした}テスト[[なんです]]。
questions.en: I'm not going out today. I've got a test tomorrow.
questions.explain: A noun needs な before んです: テストなんです.

meaning: Right? / isn't it?: looks for agreement or checks something both people know. It also softens a remark or fills a pause (そうですね…).

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}はいい{天気|てんき}です[[ね]]。
examples.en: Lovely weather today, isn't it?

examples.ja: このケーキ、おいしいです[[ね]]。
examples.en: This cake is delicious, isn't it?

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は10{時|じ}です[[ね]]。
examples.en: It's at ten tomorrow, right?

examples.ja: マリアさんは{日本語|にほんご}が{上手|じょうず}です[[ね]]。
examples.en: Your Japanese is really good, Maria.

questions.ja: 「この{店|みせ}、{安|やす}いですね。」「ええ、{本当|ほんとう}に{安|やす}いです[[ね]]。」
questions.en: "This shop is cheap, isn't it?" "Yes, it really is."
questions.explain: When you agree with something you both see, end with ね.

questions.ja: 「{何|なに}を{飲|の}みますか。」「そうです[[ね]]、じゃあ、コーヒーにします。」
questions.en: "What will you have to drink?" "Let me see… I'll have coffee, then."
questions.explain: そうですね buys a moment to think before answering.

meaning: Marks a point: a time (7時に), where something is (机の上に), a destination, or the person you give to or meet.

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}7{時|じ}[[に]]{起|お}きます。
examples.en: I get up at seven every morning.

examples.ja: {机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}[[に]]{本|ほん}があります。
examples.en: There's a book on the desk.

examples.ja: {友達|ともだち}[[に]]{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}きました。
examples.en: I wrote a letter to a friend.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}で{電車|でんしゃ}[[に]]{乗|の}りました。
examples.en: I got on the train at the station.

questions.ja: {毎晩|まいばん}11{時|じ}[[に]]{寝|ね}ます。
questions.en: I go to bed at eleven every night.
questions.explain: A clock time takes に.

questions.ja: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}の{中|なか}[[に]]{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}があります。
questions.en: There's milk in the fridge.
questions.explain: With あります and います, the place where something is takes に.

pattern: Verb-stem + に行く / Noun + に行く
meaning: Go somewhere to do something: the purpose (a verb stem or an activity noun) comes before に and a verb of movement.

examples.ja: {公園|こうえん}へ{遊|あそ}び[[に{行|い}きます]]。
examples.en: I'm going to the park to play.

examples.ja: デパートへ{服|ふく}を{買|か}い[[に{行|い}きました]]。
examples.en: I went to the department store to buy clothes.

examples.ja: {昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べ[[に{行|い}きませんか]]。
examples.en: Do you want to go and get lunch?

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、{買|か}い{物|もの}[[に{行|い}きます]]。
examples.en: I'm going shopping tomorrow.

questions.ja: {郵便局|ゆうびんきょく}へ{切手|きって}を{買|か}い[[に]]{行|い}きます。
questions.en: I'm going to the post office to buy stamps.
questions.explain: Verb-stem + に shows the purpose of going.

questions.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}に{海|うみ}へ[[{泳|およ}ぎ]]に{行|い}きました。
questions.en: On Sunday I went to the sea to swim.
questions.explain: The purpose verb goes in its ます-stem: 泳ぐ becomes 泳ぎ.

meaning: To decide on, go with: used when you choose something, such as ordering in a café or picking a day.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}はコーヒー[[にします]]。
examples.en: I'll have coffee.

examples.ja: {誕生日|たんじょうび}のプレゼントは{花|はな}[[にしました]]。
examples.en: I went with flowers for the birthday present.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}は{来月|らいげつ}[[にしましょう]]。
examples.en: Let's make the trip next month.

examples.ja: {赤|あか}いのと{青|あお}いの、どちら[[にしますか]]。
examples.en: The red one or the blue one: which will you take?

questions.ja: {昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}は{何|なに}[[にします]]か。
questions.en: What are you going to have for lunch?
questions.explain: Choosing something is Noun + にする.

questions.ja: {飲|の}み{物|もの}はオレンジジュース[[にします]]。
questions.en: For my drink, I'll have orange juice.
questions.explain: When you pick from options, the choice takes にする.

pattern: Place + に / へ + verb of movement
meaning: Both mark where you're heading. へ points to the direction; に points to the arrival point and has other jobs, like times and people, that へ can't do.

examples.ja: {来年|らいねん}、{日本|にほん}[[へ]]{行|い}きます。
examples.en: I'm going to Japan next year.

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}6{時|じ}に{家|いえ}[[に]]{帰|かえ}ります。
examples.en: I get home at six every day.

examples.ja: この{道|みち}を{北|きた}[[へ]]{行|い}ってください。
examples.en: Please go north along this road.

examples.ja: {友達|ともだち}は{昨日|きのう}アメリカ[[に]]{着|つ}きました。
examples.en: My friend arrived in America yesterday.

questions.ja: {駅|えき}で{先生|せんせい}[[に]]{会|あ}いました。
questions.en: I ran into my teacher at the station.
questions.explain: The person you meet with 会う takes に; へ only shows direction.

questions.ja: これは{母|はは}[[への]]{手紙|てがみ}です。
questions.en: This is a letter to my mother.
questions.explain: へ can take の to link to a noun (a letter to…); に can't.

meaning: Joins two nouns: whose it is (私の傘), or what kind or where from (日本語の先生). It can also stand for a noun already mentioned: 兄のです.

examples.ja: これは{私|わたし}[[の]]{傘|かさ}です。
examples.en: This is my umbrella.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}[[の]]{先生|せんせい}はとても{面白|おもしろ}いです。
examples.en: Our Japanese teacher is really fun.

examples.ja: その{青|あお}いかばんは{兄|あに}[[の]]です。
examples.en: That blue bag is my older brother's.

examples.ja: {大学|だいがく}[[の]]{友達|ともだち}と{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
examples.en: I saw a film with a friend from university.

questions.ja: あれはトムさん[[の]]{車|くるま}です。
questions.en: That's Tom's car.
questions.explain: の shows who something belongs to.

questions.ja: {学校|がっこう}[[の]]{前|まえ}に{本屋|ほんや}があります。
questions.en: There's a bookshop in front of the school.
questions.explain: Position words like 前 and 上 join the noun with の: 学校の前.

pattern: Plain form + のです (Noun / な-adjective + なのです)
meaning: Gives or asks for an explanation, like んです but fuller and more formal. Common in writing and careful speech.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}、トムさんは{会社|かいしゃ}を{休|やす}みます。{風邪|かぜ}を{引|ひ}いた[[のです]]。
examples.en: Tom is off work today. He has caught a cold.

examples.ja: この{村|むら}には{駅|えき}がありません。{村|むら}の{人|ひと}はバスで{町|まち}へ{行|い}く[[のです]]。
examples.en: This village has no station, so the people here go to town by bus.

examples.ja: どうして{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}している[[のですか]]。
examples.en: Why is it that you're studying Japanese?

examples.ja: {本当|ほんとう}は、{魚|さかな}が{嫌|きら}いな[[のです]]。
examples.en: The truth is, I don't like fish.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{毎朝|まいあさ}、{駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}きます。{体|からだ}にいい[[のです]]。
questions.en: I walk to the station every morning. It's good for my health.
questions.explain: An い-adjective takes のです directly, with no な or だ.

questions.ja: この{部屋|へや}は{駅|えき}から{近|ちか}くて、とても{便利|べんり}[[なのです]]。
questions.en: This flat is close to the station, so it's very convenient.
questions.explain: A な-adjective keeps な before のです: 便利なのです.

pattern: Verb (dictionary form) + のが下手(です)
meaning: Bad at doing something. の turns the verb into a noun so it can take が下手.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{歌|うた}を{歌|うた}う[[のが{下手|へた}]]です。
examples.en: I'm bad at singing.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}る[[のが{下手|へた}]]です。
examples.en: My father is a bad cook.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{英語|えいご}を{話|はな}す[[のが{下手|へた}]]です。
examples.en: My older brother is bad at speaking English.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{人|ひと}の{名前|なまえ}を{覚|おぼ}える[[のが{下手|へた}]]です。
examples.en: I'm bad at remembering people's names.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{泳|およ}ぐ[[のが]]{下手|へた}です。
questions.en: I'm a poor swimmer.
questions.explain: A verb needs の before が下手: 泳ぐのが下手.

questions.ja: {妹|いもうと}は{漢字|かんじ}を[[{読|よ}む]]のが{下手|へた}です。
questions.en: My younger sister is bad at reading kanji.
questions.explain: The verb before のが stays in dictionary form.

pattern: Verb (dictionary form) + のが上手(です)
meaning: Good at doing something. Mostly said about other people; said about yourself it can sound like boasting.

examples.ja: {母|はは}は{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}る[[のが{上手|じょうず}]]です。
examples.en: My mother is a good cook.

examples.ja: ケンさんは{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}る[[のが{上手|じょうず}]]ですね。
examples.en: You take great photos, Ken.

examples.ja: {弟|おとうと}は{絵|え}をかく[[のが{上手|じょうず}]]です。
examples.en: My younger brother is good at drawing.

examples.ja: マリアさんは{英語|えいご}を{教|おし}える[[のが{上手|じょうず}]]です。
examples.en: Maria is good at teaching English.

questions.ja: {姉|あね}はピアノを{弾|ひ}く[[のが]]{上手|じょうず}です。
questions.en: My older sister plays the piano well.
questions.explain: 上手 takes が, so the verb phrase becomes 弾くのが.

questions.ja: リサさんは{人|ひと}の{話|はなし}を[[{聞|き}く]]のが{上手|じょうず}です。
questions.en: Lisa is a good listener.
questions.explain: The verb before のが is in dictionary form.

pattern: Verb (dictionary form) + のが好き(です)
meaning: Like doing something. の turns the verb phrase into a noun so it can take が好き.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{本|ほん}を{読|よ}む[[のが{好|す}き]]です。
examples.en: I like reading books.

examples.ja: {妹|いもうと}は{犬|いぬ}と{遊|あそ}ぶ[[のが{好|す}き]]です。
examples.en: My younger sister loves playing with the dog.

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}に{公園|こうえん}を{歩|ある}く[[のが{好|す}き]]です。
examples.en: I like walking in the park on Sundays.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{古|ふる}い{映画|えいが}を{見|み}る[[のが{好|す}き]]です。
examples.en: My father likes watching old films.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}く[[のが]]{好|す}きです。
questions.en: I like listening to music.
questions.explain: A verb needs の to become a noun before が好き.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{友達|ともだち}と[[{話|はな}す]]のが{好|す}きです。
questions.en: I like talking with my friends.
questions.explain: Dictionary form + のが好き: 話すのが好き.

meaning: Of all the A, B is the most …. Names a group of three or more and picks the top one; also the shape of the question 〜の中で何が一番〜ですか.

examples.ja: {果物|くだもの}の{中|なか}でりんごが[[{一番|いちばん}]]{好|す}きです。
examples.en: Of all fruits, I like apples best.

examples.ja: {家族|かぞく}[[の{中|なか}で]]{父|ちち}が{一番|いちばん}{背|せ}が{高|たか}いです。
examples.en: My father is the tallest in my family.

examples.ja: {一週間|いっしゅうかん}の{中|なか}で{何曜日|なんようび}[[が]]{一番|いちばん}{忙|いそが}しいですか。
examples.en: Which day of the week are you busiest?

questions.ja: {動物|どうぶつ}の{中|なか}[[で]]{犬|いぬ}が{一番|いちばん}{好|す}きです。
questions.en: Of all animals, I like dogs best.
questions.explain: の中で sets the group you are choosing from; に, を and へ can't do that.

questions.ja: この{三|みっ}つの{中|なか}で、どれが[[{一番|いちばん}]]{安|やす}いですか。
questions.en: Of these three, which one is the cheapest?
questions.explain: Picking the top one out of three or more takes 一番.

meaning: Because / so. Gives a reason in a soft, explanatory way, which suits requests and apologies. After a noun or な-adjective it becomes なので.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っている[[ので]]、{今日|きょう}は{出|で}かけません。
examples.en: It's raining, so I'm not going out today.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}みな[[ので]]、ゆっくり{寝|ね}ます。
examples.en: Tomorrow is my day off, so I'll sleep in.

examples.ja: {頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}い[[ので]]、{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}ってもいいですか。
examples.en: I have a headache, so may I go home early?

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}は{静|しず}かな[[ので]]、よく{勉強|べんきょう}できます。
examples.en: This room is quiet, so I can study well here.

questions.ja: {風邪|かぜ}をひいた[[ので]]、{学校|がっこう}を{休|やす}みます。
questions.en: I've caught a cold, so I'm staying home from school.
questions.explain: The cold is the reason for staying home, so the link is ので, not a contrast.

questions.ja: {今日|きょう}は{日曜日|にちようび}[[なので]]、{銀行|ぎんこう}は{休|やす}みです。
questions.en: It's Sunday today, so the bank is closed.
questions.explain: After a noun, ので becomes なので; なのに would mean 'even though'.

meaning: Polite prefixes for nouns. お goes on most native Japanese words (お茶, お金) and ご on most Chinese-origin words (ご家族, ご両親); some words almost always carry one.

examples.ja: [[お]]{茶|ちゃ}をどうぞ。
examples.en: Please have some tea.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}の[[ご]]{家族|かぞく}は{何人|なんにん}ですか。
examples.en: How many people are there in your teacher's family?

examples.ja: [[お]]{名前|なまえ}は{何|なん}ですか。
examples.en: What is your name?

examples.ja: もう[[ご]]{飯|はん}を{食|た}べましたか。
examples.en: Have you eaten yet?

questions.ja: すみません、[[お]]{手洗|てあら}いはどこですか。
questions.en: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
questions.explain: 手洗い is a native word and the polite form is always お手洗い.

questions.ja: {山下|やました}さんの[[ご]]{両親|りょうしん}はお{元気|げんき}ですか。
questions.en: Are Yamashita-san's parents well?
questions.explain: 両親 is a Chinese-origin word, so it takes ご.

meaning: Marks the direct object, the thing an action is done to. With movement verbs it also marks the place you pass through or leave (道を歩く, 家を出る).

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}、コーヒー[[を]]{飲|の}みます。
examples.en: I drink coffee every morning.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}で{本|ほん}[[を]]{借|か}りました。
examples.en: I borrowed a book at the library.

examples.ja: この{道|みち}[[を]]まっすぐ{歩|ある}いてください。
examples.en: Please walk straight along this road.

examples.ja: {八時|はちじ}に{家|いえ}[[を]]{出|で}ます。
examples.en: I leave home at eight.

questions.ja: {毎晩|まいばん}、{日本語|にほんご}の{新聞|しんぶん}[[を]]{読|よ}みます。
questions.en: Every evening I read a Japanese newspaper.
questions.explain: The newspaper is what gets read, so it is the object and takes を.

questions.ja: {駅|えき}で{電車|でんしゃ}[[を]]{降|お}りました。
questions.en: I got off the train at the station.
questions.explain: 降りる marks the thing you get off with を; に goes with 乗る.

meaning: Please give me N. The everyday way to ask for or order something; a quantity goes after を: 水を二つください.

examples.ja: すみません、{水|みず}[[をください]]。
examples.en: Excuse me, some water, please.

examples.ja: このりんごを{三|みっ}つ[[ください]]。
examples.en: Three of these apples, please.

examples.ja: その{赤|あか}いかばん[[をください]]。
examples.en: I'll take that red bag, please.

questions.ja: あの{白|しろ}いシャツ[[を]]ください。
questions.en: That white shirt, please.
questions.explain: The thing you ask for is the object of ください, so it takes を.

questions.ja: {切手|きって}を{三枚|さんまい}[[ください]]。
questions.en: Three stamps, please.
questions.explain: Noun + を + amount + ください asks for things; を comes once, before the amount, and てください follows a verb.

meaning: However. Opens a sentence that goes against the one before it. Formal and mostly written; in conversation でも is more usual.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{安|やす}いです。[[しかし]]、あまりおいしくないです。
examples.en: This place is cheap. However, the food isn't very good.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}は{難|むずか}しいです。[[しかし]]、とても{面白|おもしろ}いです。
examples.en: Japanese is difficult. However, it's very interesting.

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}しました。[[しかし]]、テストはよくできませんでした。
examples.en: I practised every day. However, the test went badly.

questions.ja: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}みました。[[しかし]]、まだ{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}いです。
questions.en: I took some medicine. However, my head still hurts.
questions.explain: The headache continuing goes against what you'd expect, so a contrast word is needed.

questions.ja: {山下|やました}さんは{料理|りょうり}が{好|す}きです。[[しかし]]、あまり{上手|じょうず}じゃありません。
questions.en: Yamashita-san likes cooking. However, she isn't very good at it.
questions.explain: Liking it but not being good at it is a contrast, which しかし introduces.

meaning: And then / after that. Puts the next action in order, and can also add one more item to a list (and also).

examples.ja: {朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べました。[[それから]]、{学校|がっこう}へ{行|い}きました。
examples.en: I had breakfast. Then I went to school.

examples.ja: {宿題|しゅくだい}をして、[[それから]]テレビを{見|み}ます。
examples.en: I'll do my homework, and after that I'll watch TV.

examples.ja: ペンとノート、[[それから]]{辞書|じしょ}を{持|も}ってきてください。
examples.en: Please bring a pen, a notebook, and also a dictionary.

questions.ja: {駅|えき}で{友達|ともだち}に{会|あ}いました。[[それから]]、{一緒|いっしょ}に{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
questions.en: I met a friend at the station. After that, we saw a movie together.
questions.explain: The movie simply comes next, so the link is それから, not a contrast.

questions.ja: {手|て}を{洗|あら}って、[[それから]]ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べましょう。
questions.en: Let's wash our hands, and then eat.
questions.explain: Eating follows washing in time, which それから expresses.

meaning: And / and then. Joins two sentences to add another point or the next event; a little more formal than それから.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}は{広|ひろ}いです。[[そして]]、とても{明|あか}るいです。
examples.en: This room is spacious. And it's very bright.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}はデパートへ{行|い}きました。[[そして]]、{新|あたら}しい{靴|くつ}を{買|か}いました。
examples.en: Yesterday I went to a department store. And I bought new shoes.

examples.ja: {山下|やました}さんは{頭|あたま}がいいです。[[そして]]、スポーツも{上手|じょうず}です。
examples.en: Yamashita-san is smart. And she's good at sports too.

questions.ja: この{町|まち}は{静|しず}かです。[[そして]]、{緑|みどり}が{多|おお}いです。
questions.en: This town is quiet. And it has lots of greenery.
questions.explain: The second sentence adds another good point, so そして fits; there's no contrast or cause.

questions.ja: {弟|おとうと}は{英語|えいご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しています。[[そして]]、{中国語|ちゅうごくご}も{勉強|べんきょう}しています。
questions.en: My younger brother is studying English. And he's studying Chinese too.
questions.explain: も adds one more thing to the first fact, which is what そして does.

meaning: Too / too much. Attach to a verb stem (食べすぎる) or an adjective stem (高すぎる, 静かすぎる) to say something goes past the right amount. It conjugates like an ichidan verb.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}の{夜|よる}、{食|た}べ[[すぎました]]。
examples.en: I ate too much last night.

examples.ja: このかばんは{高|たか}[[すぎます]]。
examples.en: This bag is too expensive.

examples.ja: この{問題|もんだい}は{難|むずか}し[[すぎて]]、わかりません。
examples.en: This question is too hard; I don't get it.

examples.ja: テレビを{見|み}[[すぎる]]のは{目|め}に{悪|わる}いです。
examples.en: Watching too much TV is bad for your eyes.

questions.ja: このスープは[[{熱|あつ}すぎます]]。
questions.en: This soup is too hot.
questions.explain: Drop the final い of an い-adjective, then add すぎます.

questions.ja: {昨日|きのう}は[[{歩|ある}きすぎて]]、{足|あし}が{痛|いた}いです。
questions.en: I walked too much yesterday, so my legs hurt.
questions.explain: すぎる attaches to the ます-stem: 歩き + すぎて.

pattern: 〜たことがある / 〜たことがあります
meaning: Have done (at some point). Talks about experience, something that has happened to you at least once; たことがない means 'have never'.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}へ{行|い}った[[ことがあります]]。
examples.en: I have been to Japan.

examples.ja: すしを{食|た}べた[[ことがあります]]か。
examples.en: Have you ever eaten sushi?

examples.ja: {私|わたし}はまだ{飛行機|ひこうき}に{乗|の}った[[ことがありません]]。
examples.en: I've never been on a plane yet.

questions.ja: {日本|にほん}の{歌|うた}を[[{歌|うた}った]]ことがありますか。
questions.en: Have you ever sung a Japanese song?
questions.explain: Experience uses the plain past (た-form) before ことがある.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{一度|いちど}も{海|うみ}で{泳|およ}いだことが[[ありません]]。
questions.en: I have never once swum in the sea.
questions.explain: 一度も needs a negative, and the verb in this pattern is always ある.

meaning: Want to (do). Attach to a verb stem to say what you want to do; it conjugates like an い-adjective (たくない, たかった). Used for yourself, or when asking someone directly.

examples.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みに{海|うみ}へ{行|い}き[[たい]]です。
examples.en: I want to go to the beach over the summer holidays.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{何|なに}も{食|た}べ[[たくない]]です。
examples.en: I don't want to eat anything today.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}のとき、{先生|せんせい}になり[[たかった]]です。
examples.en: When I was a child, I wanted to be a teacher.

examples.ja: {何|なに}が{飲|の}み[[たい]]ですか。
examples.en: What would you like to drink?

questions.ja: {新|あたら}しいパソコンを{買|か}い[[たい]]です。
questions.en: I want to buy a new computer.
questions.explain: Wanting to do something is verb stem + たい; ほしい goes after a noun.

questions.ja: {疲|つか}れたので、{今日|きょう}はどこへも{行|い}き[[たくない]]です。
questions.en: I'm tired, so I don't want to go anywhere today.
questions.explain: たい makes its negative like an い-adjective: たい becomes たくない.

meaning: Do things like A and B. Gives a couple of example actions out of many, in no set order; the list ends with する.

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}は{本|ほん}を{読|よ}ん[[だり]]、{音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}いたりします。
examples.en: On Sundays I do things like reading and listening to music.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{掃除|そうじ}をしたり、{洗濯|せんたく}をし[[たり]]します。
examples.en: On my days off I do things like cleaning and laundry.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{友達|ともだち}と{買|か}い{物|もの}をしたり、{映画|えいが}を{見|み}たり[[しました]]。
examples.en: Yesterday I went shopping, saw a movie and so on with friends.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}たちが{公園|こうえん}で{走|はし}っ[[たり]]、{遊|あそ}んだりしています。
examples.en: The children are running around and playing in the park.

questions.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みは{山|やま}に{登|のぼ}ったり、{川|かわ}で{泳|およ}い[[だり]]しました。
questions.en: Over the summer holidays I did things like climbing mountains and swimming in rivers.
questions.explain: たり is built from the た-form, and 泳ぐ becomes 泳いだ, so 泳いだり.

questions.ja: {夜|よる}は、テレビを[[{見|み}たり]]、{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}いたりします。
questions.en: In the evenings I do things like watching TV and writing letters.
questions.explain: Take the た-form (見た) and add り: 見たり.

meaning: Has been done (and stays that way). A transitive verb + てある describes a state someone set up on purpose, often ready for later; the thing usually takes が: 窓が開けてある.

examples.ja: {窓|まど}が{開|あ}け[[てあります]]。
examples.en: The window has been left open.

examples.ja: {机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}に{花|はな}が{置|お}い[[てあります]]。
examples.en: Some flowers have been put on the desk.

examples.ja: ドアに{名前|なまえ}が{書|か}い[[てあります]]。
examples.en: There's a name written on the door.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{切符|きっぷ}はもう{買|か}っ[[てあります]]よ。
examples.en: I've already got tomorrow's tickets.

questions.ja: {寒|さむ}いので、{窓|まど}が{閉|し}め[[てあります]]。
questions.en: It's cold, so the windows have been shut.
questions.explain: With が and a transitive verb like 閉める, a state someone set up is てある.

questions.ja: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}にジュースが{入|い}れて[[あります]]。
questions.en: Some juice has been put in the fridge.
questions.explain: 入れる is transitive, so 'juice has been put in' with が is 入れてあります.

meaning: Is doing / is in a state. Shows an action in progress (食べている), a habit (毎日走っている), or a state left by a change (結婚している, 住んでいる).

examples.ja: {今|いま}、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っ[[ています]]。
examples.en: It's raining now.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{銀行|ぎんこう}で{働|はたら}い[[ています]]。
examples.en: My older brother works at a bank.

examples.ja: {山下|やました}さんは{結婚|けっこん}し[[ています]]か。
examples.en: Is Yamashita-san married?

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}、{公園|こうえん}を{走|はし}っ[[ています]]。
examples.en: I go running in the park every morning.

questions.ja: {母|はは}は{今|いま}、{台所|だいどころ}で{料理|りょうり}を[[{作|つく}っています]]。
questions.en: My mother is cooking in the kitchen right now.
questions.explain: 作る has the て-form 作って, then add います.

questions.ja: {姉|あね}は{去年|きょねん}から{外国|がいこく}に[[{住|す}んでいます]]。
questions.en: My older sister has been living abroad since last year.
questions.explain: Living somewhere from a past point until now is a state: 住んでいます.

meaning: After doing A, then B. Stresses that B only happens once A is finished; with a length of time it also means 'since' (日本に来てから).

examples.ja: {歯|は}を{磨|みが}い[[てから]]、{寝|ね}ます。
examples.en: I brush my teeth before I go to bed.

examples.ja: {電話|でんわ}をかけ[[てから]]、{友達|ともだち}の{家|いえ}へ{行|い}きます。
examples.en: I'll call first, then go over to my friend's house.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}に{来|き}[[てから]]、もう{二年|にねん}になります。
examples.en: It's been two years since I came to Japan.

questions.ja: {薬|くすり}を[[{飲|の}んでから]]、{寝|ね}てください。
questions.en: Please take the medicine and then go to sleep.
questions.explain: てから follows the て-form, and 飲む becomes 飲んで.

questions.ja: {宿題|しゅくだい}が[[{終|お}わってから]]、{遊|あそ}びに{行|い}きます。
questions.en: I'll go out to play after my homework is finished.
questions.explain: Use the て-form 終わって + から; 前に would need the dictionary form.

meaning: Please do …. A polite request or instruction, made with the て-form of a verb.

examples.ja: もう{少|すこ}しゆっくり{話|はな}し[[てください]]。
examples.en: Please speak a little more slowly.

examples.ja: ここに{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}い[[てください]]。
examples.en: Please write your name here.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{八時|はちじ}に{来|き}[[てください]]。
examples.en: Please come at eight tomorrow.

examples.ja: すみません、{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}っ[[てください]]。
examples.en: Excuse me, could you take a photo for us?

questions.ja: {暑|あつ}いですね。{窓|まど}を[[{開|あ}けて]]ください。
questions.en: It's hot, isn't it? Please open the window.
questions.explain: ください after a verb needs the て-form: 開けて.

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}を{出|で}るとき、{電気|でんき}を[[{消|け}して]]ください。
questions.en: Please turn off the light when you leave the room.
questions.explain: Verbs ending in す make the て-form with して: 消して.

pattern: 〜てはいけない / 〜てはいけません
meaning: Must not / not allowed. The て-form + はいけない forbids something: rules, signs and warnings.

examples.ja: ここで{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}っ[[てはいけません]]。
examples.en: You mustn't take photos here.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}で{大|おお}きい{声|こえ}で{話|はな}し[[てはいけません]]。
examples.en: You mustn't talk loudly in the library.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}はお{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}ん[[ではいけません]]。
examples.en: Children must not drink alcohol.

questions.ja: テストのとき、{辞書|じしょ}を[[{使|つか}っては]]いけません。
questions.en: You mustn't use a dictionary during the test.
questions.explain: 使う has the て-form 使って, then add はいけません.

questions.ja: {危|あぶ}ないですから、この{川|かわ}で{泳|およ}い[[ではいけません]]。
questions.en: It's dangerous, so you mustn't swim in this river.
questions.explain: Because it's dangerous, swimming is forbidden: 泳いではいけません.

meaning: May / it's OK to. The て-form + もいい gives permission; as a question (〜てもいいですか) it asks for it.

examples.ja: ここに{座|すわ}っ[[てもいいです]]か。
examples.en: May I sit here?

examples.ja: {窓|まど}を{開|あ}け[[てもいいです]]か。
examples.en: Is it all right if I open the window?

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}ん[[でもいいです]]よ。
examples.en: You can take tomorrow off.

examples.ja: このペンを{使|つか}っ[[てもいいです]]。
examples.en: You may use this pen.

questions.ja: すみません、トイレを{借|か}り[[てもいいです]]か。
questions.en: Excuse me, may I use the bathroom?
questions.explain: 借りる is a る-verb, so 借りて + もいいです.

questions.ja: この{本|ほん}を{少|すこ}し[[{読|よ}んでも]]いいですか。
questions.en: May I read this book for a bit?
questions.explain: 読む has the て-form 読んで, and permission uses も: 読んでもいい.

meaning: And / with. Joins nouns into a complete list (A and B, nothing else), or marks the person you do something with.

examples.ja: {机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}にペン[[と]]ノートがあります。
examples.en: There's a pen and a notebook on the desk.

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}に{友達|ともだち}[[と]]{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
examples.en: I saw a movie with a friend on Sunday.

examples.ja: {母|はは}[[と]]{一緒|いっしょ}に{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}きます。
examples.en: I'm going shopping with my mother.

examples.ja: コーヒー[[と]]ケーキをください。
examples.en: A coffee and a piece of cake, please.

questions.ja: {昨日|きのう}、{兄|あに}[[と]]{一緒|いっしょ}にテニスをしました。
questions.en: Yesterday I played tennis with my older brother.
questions.explain: The person you do something with takes と, often with 一緒に.

questions.ja: {家族|かぞく}は{父|ちち}[[と]]{母|はは}と{私|わたし}の{三人|さんにん}です。
questions.en: There are three of us in my family: my father, my mother and me.
questions.explain: The list is complete (three people), so it's と; や would hint at others.

meaning: When / at the time. Ties an event to a time or situation; it follows plain verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives with な, and nouns with の.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}の[[とき]]、よくこの{公園|こうえん}で{遊|あそ}びました。
examples.en: When I was a child, I often played in this park.

examples.ja: {暇|ひま}な[[とき]]、{何|なに}をしますか。
examples.en: What do you do when you have free time?

examples.ja: {寒|さむ}い[[とき]]は、{温|あたた}かいお{茶|ちゃ}を{飲|の}みます。
examples.en: When it's cold, I drink hot tea.

examples.ja: {家|いえ}を{出|で}る[[とき]]、「いってきます」と{言|い}います。
examples.en: When I leave the house, I say "ittekimasu".

questions.ja: {学生|がくせい}[[の]]とき、{毎日|まいにち}{図書館|としょかん}へ{行|い}きました。
questions.en: When I was a student, I went to the library every day.
questions.explain: A noun joins とき with の: 学生のとき.

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}が[[{静|しず}かな]]とき、{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みます。
questions.en: When my room is quiet, I read.
questions.explain: A な-adjective keeps な before とき: 静かなとき.

meaning: Very. Adds emphasis to an adjective or a feeling verb (とても好き) in positive sentences; for 'not very', use あまり〜ない instead.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}は[[とても]]{面白|おもしろ}いです。
examples.en: This book is really interesting.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は[[とても]]{暑|あつ}いですね。
examples.en: It's very hot today, isn't it?

examples.ja: {山下|やました}さんの{部屋|へや}は[[とても]]きれいです。
examples.en: Yamashita-san's room is very tidy.

questions.ja: この{料理|りょうり}は[[とても]]おいしいです。
questions.en: This dish is very tasty.
questions.explain: The sentence is positive; あまり, 少しも and 何も all need a negative.

questions.ja: この{店|みせ}は[[とても]]{有名|ゆうめい}です。
questions.en: This shop is very famous.
questions.explain: To say 'very' before an adjective, use とても; たくさん and おおぜい count amounts.

pattern: 〜つもりです / 〜ないつもりです
meaning: Intend to / plan to. After a plain verb it says what you have decided to do; after ない, what you plan not to do.

examples.ja: {来年|らいねん}、{日本|にほん}へ{行|い}く[[つもり]]です。
examples.en: I'm planning to go to Japan next year.

examples.ja: {今晩|こんばん}は{何|なに}も{食|た}べない[[つもり]]です。
examples.en: I intend not to eat anything tonight.

examples.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みは{何|なに}をする[[つもり]]ですか。
examples.en: What are you planning to do over the summer holidays?

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{車|くるま}を{買|か}う[[つもり]]でしたが、{買|か}いませんでした。
examples.en: I was going to buy a new car, but I didn't.

questions.ja: {来月|らいげつ}から{毎朝|まいあさ}[[{走|はし}る]]つもりです。
questions.en: I plan to go running every morning from next month.
questions.explain: つもり follows the plain dictionary form: 走るつもり.

questions.ja: {大学|だいがく}を{出|で}てから、{銀行|ぎんこう}で{働|はたら}く[[つもり]]です。
questions.en: After I finish university, I plan to work at a bank.
questions.explain: After the dictionary form 働く, only つもり fits; たい and ましょう need the ます-stem.

meaning: Marks the topic, what the sentence is about ('as for N'), and can also set one thing against another. Written は but said わ.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}[[は]]{学生|がくせい}です。
examples.en: I'm a student.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}[[は]]{暑|あつ}いですね。
examples.en: It's hot today, isn't it?

examples.ja: {肉|にく}は{食|た}べますが、{魚|さかな}[[は]]{食|た}べません。
examples.en: I eat meat, but I don't eat fish.

examples.ja: トイレ[[は]]どこですか。
examples.en: Where is the restroom?

questions.ja: {明日|あした}[[は]]{何曜日|なんようび}ですか。
questions.en: What day of the week is tomorrow?
questions.explain: 明日 is the topic you're asking about, so it takes は.

questions.ja: {兄|あに}は{背|せ}が{高|たか}いですが、{私|わたし}[[は]]{低|ひく}いです。
questions.en: My older brother is tall, but I'm short.
questions.explain: は sets 私 against 兄; も ('also') would contradict the contrast.

meaning: A is more … than B. Takes A as the topic and compares it with B; より marks the thing you measure against.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{昨日|きのう}[[より]]{寒|さむ}いです。
examples.en: Today is colder than yesterday.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}はバス[[より]]{速|はや}いです。
examples.en: Trains are faster than buses.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{父|ちち}[[より]]{背|せ}が{高|たか}いです。
examples.en: My older brother is taller than my father.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}は{英語|えいご}[[より]]{難|むずか}しいですか。
examples.en: Is Japanese harder than English?

questions.ja: {飛行機|ひこうき}は{電車|でんしゃ}[[より]]{高|たか}いです。
questions.en: Planes are more expensive than trains.
questions.explain: より marks what you compare against; ほど only works with a negative.

questions.ja: このかばんは、あのかばん[[より]]{軽|かる}いです。
questions.en: This bag is lighter than that one.
questions.explain: The bag being compared against takes より.

meaning: How is N? / How about N? Asks for someone's opinion or impression, or makes a gentle suggestion; いかがですか is the more polite version.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{仕事|しごと}[[はどうですか]]。
examples.en: How's the new job?

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}の{食|た}べ{物|もの}[[はどうですか]]。
examples.en: How do you find Japanese food?

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}[[はどうでしたか]]。
examples.en: How was your trip?

examples.ja: コーヒー[[はどうですか]]。
examples.en: Would you like some coffee?

questions.ja: {新|あたら}しいアパートは[[どう]]ですか。
questions.en: How's your new apartment?
questions.explain: To ask what something is like, use どう; どの needs a noun after it.

questions.ja: {今週|こんしゅう}は{忙|いそが}しいです。{来週|らいしゅう}[[は]]どうですか。
questions.en: I'm busy this week. How about next week?
questions.explain: The thing you suggest or ask about is the topic: 来週はどうですか.

meaning: A, B and so on. Lists a few examples from a bigger group, hinting there are more; often followed by など.

examples.ja: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}に{卵|たまご}[[や]]{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}があります。
examples.en: There are eggs, milk and other things in the fridge.

examples.ja: かばんの{中|なか}に{財布|さいふ}[[や]]{鍵|かぎ}などが{入|はい}っています。
examples.en: My bag has my wallet, keys and so on in it.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{公園|こうえん}[[や]]{図書館|としょかん}へ{行|い}きます。
examples.en: On my days off I go to places like the park and the library.

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}にテレビ[[や]]ベッドなどがあります。
questions.en: There's a TV, a bed and so on in the room.
questions.explain: や links nouns as examples from a longer list, which など confirms.

questions.ja: スーパーで{肉|にく}[[や]]{野菜|やさい}などを{買|か}いました。
questions.en: I bought meat, vegetables and other things at the supermarket.
questions.explain: Two example items joined before など take や.

meaning: Sentence-ending particle for telling the listener something they don't know or should notice, like 'you know' or 'I tell you'. ね, by contrast, looks for agreement.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}のラーメンはおいしいです[[よ]]。
examples.en: The ramen at this place is good, you know.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}はもう{出|で}ました[[よ]]。
examples.en: The train has already left, I'm afraid.

examples.ja: あ、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っています[[よ]]。
examples.en: Oh, look, it's raining.

examples.ja: {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です[[よ]]。
examples.en: It's fine, really.

questions.ja: {知|し}らないんですか。{明日|あした}はテストです[[よ]]。
questions.en: You didn't know? There's a test tomorrow!
questions.explain: The listener doesn't know about the test, so you tell them with よ; ね assumes they already know.

questions.ja: 「この{近|ちか}くに{銀行|ぎんこう}はありますか。」「ええ、{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}にあります[[よ]]。」
questions.en: "Is there a bank near here?" "Yes, there's one in front of the station."
questions.explain: The answer gives the asker new information, which is what よ is for.

meaning: B is more … than A. Compares two things and puts the focus on the one that comes out ahead; also the usual answer to どちらが〜ですか.

examples.ja: {肉|にく}より{魚|さかな}の[[ほうが]]{好|す}きです。
examples.en: I like fish more than meat.

examples.ja: この{町|まち}は、{昼|ひる}より{夜|よる}の[[ほうが]]にぎやかです。
examples.en: This town is livelier at night than during the day.

examples.ja: 「コーヒーと{紅茶|こうちゃ}と、どちらがいいですか。」「{紅茶|こうちゃ}の[[ほうが]]いいです。」
examples.en: "Which would you like, coffee or tea?" "I'd prefer tea."

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}で{行|い}く[[より]]、みんなで{行|い}くほうが{楽|たの}しいです。
examples.en: Going with everyone is more fun than going alone.

questions.ja: {自転車|じてんしゃ}より{車|くるま}の[[ほうが]]{速|はや}いです。
questions.en: Cars are faster than bicycles.
questions.explain: The winner of the comparison is marked with のほうが.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{犬|いぬ}[[より]]{猫|ねこ}のほうが{好|す}きです。
questions.en: I like cats more than dogs.
questions.explain: より marks the thing that loses the comparison.

meaning: 'While / during': the main action goes on for the whole stretch of time. Attaches to Verb-ている, an adjective, or noun + の.
'While / during', but the main action happens at one point inside that stretch instead of filling all of it (which is plain 間). Same attachments as 間.
With a negative verb or adjective: 'not very / not much'. A soft, partial negative, not a total denial.
'After': Verb-た form or noun + の + あとで. The main action follows once the first one is over.
Conditional 'if': verbs change the final -u to -eba (行けば), i-adjectives take -ければ. Sets a condition and the result that follows; common for general truths and hypotheticals.
'In the case of / if it happens that', for situations that may come up, typical of rules and instructions. Plain form, noun + の, or na-adjective + な.
Noun + ばかり: 'nothing but / only that', usually hinting there is too much of one thing (eats only meat, nothing but complaints).
'Just by / with only': one small thing on its own is enough to bring the result (just thinking about it is fun). Plain verb or noun + だけで.
Verb stem + 出す: something starts suddenly or bursts out, 'break into / start to' (burst out crying, suddenly started raining).
A very polite です, used by staff to customers and in formal announcements. Replaces です after nouns and na-adjectives.
Noun + でも: 'even' (even a child knows that), or a soft 'or something' in offers (coffee or something?). Not ても, which follows a verb's て form, and not the 'but' that opens a sentence.
Formal or written 'isn't it? / surely': presents something as obvious and invites agreement, or a surprised 'why, it's ...!'. The stiff counterpart of じゃないか.
Noun + が必要だ: '~ is needed'. Names the thing required; the person or purpose takes に or には.
Noun + がする for something you sense: a smell, sound, taste or feeling is noticed (it smells good, I hear a noise, I have a feeling).
Adjective stem + がり (often + 屋): a noun for someone who easily feels that way, like 'someone who's always cold' or 'a scaredy-cat'. A light, slightly teasing label.
Adjective stem (or たい stem) + がる: describes someone else's feelings or wishes from how they act ('acts scared', 'seems to want'). ている form for the current state.
A very polite あります, 'there is / we have', used in service and formal speech (the restroom is over there). Different from でございます, which replaces です.
Verb stem + 始める: 'start to / begin doing'. A neutral beginning of an action or change; compare 出す, which is sudden.
'Should be / is supposed to': a confident conclusion from facts or reasoning. Plain form, noun + の, or na-adjective + な.
'There's no way that / it can't be': the speaker reasons that something is impossible. The firm opposite of はずだ.
Dictionary form + 必要がある: 'need to / it's necessary to do'. 必要はない means 'there's no need to'. Takes a verb, while が必要 takes a noun.
Volitional form: godan verbs change -u to -ou (行こう), ichidan verbs swap る for よう (食べよう), する becomes しよう. Means 'let's' or 'I'll'; the polite version is ましょう.
Honorific verb for いる, 行く and 来る, used for the listener or someone you respect. Polite form is いらっしゃいます.
Humble polite form of します, for your own actions toward a customer or superior. Often in お / ご + verb + いたします.
Casual 'isn't it? / come on': insists something is obvious, scolds, or shows surprise ('hey, it's you!'). Sounds blunt and a bit masculine; ではないか is the formal version.
'Whether or not', for an embedded yes-no question: plain form + かどうか + know, ask, decide. Nouns and na-adjectives drop だ.
Sentence-final 'I wonder', soft and traditionally feminine. Does the same job as かな.
Casual ending for yes-no questions, warm or a little old-fashioned, mostly from male or older speakers. Plain form + かい.
'Might / may': possible but not certain. Plain form; nouns and na-adjectives drop だ. Polite: かもしれません.
Sentence-final 'I wonder', thinking aloud or softening a question. Casual and used by everyone, while かしら sounds feminine.
'Made from': the raw material is changed and can't be seen in the result (wine from grapes). With で作る the material is still visible.
'Surely / I bet': strong confidence in a guess or wish, often with だろう or と思う. Surer than たぶん.
'Around / about' a time. ごろ follows a clock time or date (around 3 o'clock); ころ follows a phrase or noun + の for a period (back when I was a child).
Plain verb + こと: turns a verb or clause into a noun, 'doing / the act of', so it can be a subject or object. The base of ことができる, ことがある and more.
Dictionary or ない form + ことがある: 'there are times when / sometimes'. Not たことがある with past た, which means 'have done before'.
Dictionary form + ことができる: 'can / be able to'. A bit more formal than the potential form; also for what's allowed (you can pay by card).
Dictionary or ない form + ことになる: 'it's been decided / it turns out that', when others or circumstances decide. ことにする is your own decision.
Dictionary or ない form + ことにする: 'decide to', a choice the speaker makes. ことにしている is a rule you keep for yourself.
I-adjective stem + くする: 'make something (more) ~' on purpose (make the room warmer, make it shorter). Na-adjectives and nouns use にする.
'Suddenly / all of a sudden', for an abrupt, unexpected change (it suddenly got cold, stopped without warning).
'By' a deadline: the action happens at some point before then. まで alone means 'until', the action lasting up to that time.
'As it is / unchanged': a state stays the same while something else happens (slept with the light on). Verb-た, ない form, noun + の, or adjective.
Formal 'or' between choices in notices, forms and instructions. In speech, か or それとも is more usual.
Casual 'seems / looks like': a guess from what you see or hear, or a comparison (it's like a dream). Plain form or noun directly, no の needed.
〜みたいな + noun: 'a [thing] like ~', describing or giving an example (a person like you). The adjective form of みたいだ.
〜みたいに + verb or adjective: 'like / as if', describing how something is done (sings like a pro). The adverb form of みたいだ.
Number + counter + も: 'as many as / as much as', stressing that the amount feels large (waited three whole hours). With a negative, 一つも〜ない is 'not even one'.
Dictionary form + な: a blunt 'don't!'. Rough and mostly male; seen on signs and in strong warnings. Much harsher than ないで.
'And so on / such as': picks examples from a longer list, or softens a single example. More formal than とか.
Verb stem + ながら: 'while doing', two actions by the same person at once. The main action comes last (study while listening to music).
With a negative: 'not easily / just won't', something takes longer or is harder than hoped (the bus just won't come).
ない form, drop い, add ければいけない: 'must / have to'. Leans toward personal or situational need; common in speech. Casual: なきゃ.
